So to me, significant design methodology changes or technical advancement seems to be the reasonable way to describe eras of game style, because... The others are subjective and useless for any kind of helpful classification. "When I was a kid" won't help future games historians
If someone told you "I am making a game like half life" and then showed people Doom, you, and everybody else, would very understandably go "that's not what I had in my head when you said half life"

Like if you saw someone say that Doom and Half life were from the same era of game, most people would pretty reasonably point out how they're very different in terms of visuals and design. Most people would disagree with you.

Some people think of an era of games as "games that I liked between these two points in time" or "games that came out when I was at a certain point in my life"

Wouldn't it be easier to think of it in terms of technology? Or identifying points where there's a major shift? Eg 2.5d to 3d
